title: AI television is here. And it sucks
gist: Imogen West-Knights reviews No Big Deal, billed as the first fully AI-produced sitcom (human-written, AI-generated visuals and actors) on YouTube, and finds it uncanny and bad. She notes AI in TV is mostly back-end today, union protections from Sag-Aftra and Equity hold back AI actors, but AI is already displacing actors in the roughly $1.3bn mobile microdrama market.

insights.claim: No Big Deal, created and written by Andrew Dickinson and premiered on YouTube, is billed as the first fully AI-produced sitcom: a human-written workplace comedy about venture capitalists with all visual elements, including actors, generated by AI.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Marks the arrival of end-to-end generative video in long-form scripted entertainment.
insights.locator: It gives me no pleasure to report

insights.claim: West-Knights finds the show terrible despite a passable script: uncanny smooth faces, flat vocal delivery, a warped French accent and bland, empty AI-generated sets.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Current AI video quality is not yet competitive for premium scripted TV; human-performance moats persist near term.
insights.quote: There is an uncanny smoothness about their appearances, a flatness to the vocal delivery

insights.claim: Dickinson reportedly used AI to save money; West-Knights argues the costs of actors, locations and crews remain indispensable for making a good show.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Cost-cutting via AI trades off quality; production budgets for premium content unlikely to collapse yet.
insights.quote: You can, plainly, now make a TV show with AI.

insights.claim: In TV, AI is mostly used for back-end work — visual effects, editing, picture quality — and, per industry reports, increasingly in casting, R&D and production scheduling, but few AI-generated actors appear on screen yet.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Near-term AI value in media accrues to production tooling and post-production rather than synthetic talent.
insights.locator: The staggering badness of this one

insights.claim: Use of AI-generated actors provokes unease and backlash, as with the use of the late Val Kilmer's likeness in the film As Deep as the Grave.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Reputational risk constrains studios' use of synthetic likenesses.
insights.locator: The staggering badness of this one

insights.claim: AI video has improved enormously since the Will Smith spaghetti video of about three years ago and, while not yet realistic, indistinguishable AI actors are 'surely coming'; union protections won by Sag-Aftra and Equity are the main barrier, and their future robustness is uncertain.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Labour agreements are the key gating factor for synthetic-actor adoption; watch future union negotiations.
insights.quote: For now, the answer is union protections

insights.claim: With YouTube increasingly seen as the new television by viewership, what legacy TV studios do about AI may matter less and less.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Platform shift to YouTube weakens legacy studios and union leverage over AI use.

insights.claim: AI replacement of actors is already happening in microdramas or 'verticals' — short-form phone-native narrative series — an industry worth around $1.3bn, where a Business Insider investigation found actors being dropped from booked jobs for AI replacements.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Low-budget, mobile-first formats are the first market where generative video displaces human labour at scale.
insights.quote: This is a gigantic industry, worth something like $1.3bn dollars

insights.claim: Audiences will watch AI-generated narrative content: a Love Island-style TikTok series featuring hybrid human-fruit creatures was hugely popular.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Demand exists for AI-native content on social platforms, regardless of critical quality.
insights.quote: People will watch AI-generated narrative content.

insights.claim: West-Knights hopes great acting retains an irreducible human nuance — exemplified by Julia Roberts' wordless casino-floor walk in Ocean's Eleven — that AI cannot match, and on No Big Deal's evidence it is 'not even close'.
insights.speaker: Imogen West-Knights
insights.so_what: Premium talent may retain pricing power if subtle performance remains beyond AI.
insights.quote: On the evidence of No Big Deal, not even close.
insights.locator: Can AI deliver that kind of nuance
